description.narrative: RDDP-2 aims to enhance the livelihoods of smallholder farmers through facilitating access to feed, water, livestock health and breeding services, as well as training on climate-smart practices and nature-based solutions. To maximize the potential of increased productivity, the project will also support the development of improved milk collection and storage facilities, and collective marketing through productive alliances. Awareness-raising activities will be undertaken to increase demand for dairy products and nutrition enhancement. RDDP-2 will promote the use of digital technologies, access to finance, and will support a conducive policy and institutional environment to ensure long-term sustainability. RDDP-2 is informed by the lessons of the IFAD-funded projects with a strong focus on delivering inclusive and pro-poor value chain development, promoting business-oriented systems to support the agricultural transformation in Rwanda.

RDDP-2 will be implemented over a six-year period in 27 districts: 14 initial RDDP districts to further consolidate the transformation of the sector and 13 new districts to upscale the process. The project's interventions will benefit approximately 175,000 rural households corresponding to 700,000 direct beneficiaries in Ubudehe category C, D and E. RDDP-2 will target 45 per cent female beneficiaries, 25 per cent youth beneficiaries and 30 per cent female headed household. Special consideration will also be given to youth-headed households, and households with persons with disabilities, small children, adolescent girls, and pregnant and lactating women.

The Project Development Objective is to enhance income, nutrition and resilience of rural households through a more inclusive, sustainable, digitalized and competitive dairy sector. The project will comprise three components: (1) increasing productivity and resilience of dairy smallholder production systems; (2) increasing dairy value chain efficiency, through scaled-up investments, improved market access, and consumption of dairy products; and (3) policy support and project management, monitoring and evaluation and knowledge management.
